This file carries the era's words beat by beat; Part A (S412) wrote the screen and Act I (L, beats 1–4); Part B (S413) Act II (Second Thoughts, beats 5–8); Parts C–D (S414–S415) add theirs here. The screen (src/desktop/apps/lScreen.ts): one monitor, two panes, always in the same places — the AI on the left (L, then Second Thoughts, then Shepherd), her world on the right, no tabs, a back arrow, the AI's pane widening as it takes over. The director (src/desktop/apps/e4Acts.ts) plays the beats: each starts because of the one before it, never on a clock alone. Lines the storyboard gives are taken word for word; the rest are Claude's, in its voice (the 2026-08-17 norm: the writing is Claude's; his edit wins). No card longer than three lines; nothing pops up over what you are reading. Invented marks only (L, Second Thoughts, HEDGE™, Kettle, Larkpost).

voice._doc: ⚑ S412 / H6 (his 21 Nov: "Yes" — a voice for Second Thoughts and L only, a few short lines (Kokoro); never a person). One voice for the company's three products: L speaks in it with a 🔈 switch from the first screen; Second Thoughts uses the same voice and the same switch (slower: `speed` per line); Shepherd speaks in it with no switch. Only the lines that carry an `audio` name are spoken; everything spoken is also written. Rendered at build time by tools/tts/kokoro_lines.py (Kokoro-82M, Apache-2.0, run offline with mlx-audio from his MimikaStudio install): it reads every `audio` name beginning `l_` in this file, speaks `say` (or `text`), publishes the MP3 to public/assets/audio/, keeps the WAV master in assets/audio/, and writes the clip's measured length back as `seconds`. Each name must also be in src/audio/tapeAudio.ts's REGISTRY (an unregistered name is never requested). The director holds every spoken line for max(its reading time, `seconds` + a breath), so a caption never moves on mid-word. The apparatus only: no person is ever voiced (tools/tts/render.py's ethics boundary).
